summary: Training volume over the last 4 weeks has been inconsistent and notably low, with only 8 logged sessions and significant gaps suggesting missed training days. Sleep quality is a serious concern — multiple nights under 4 hours (186, 205, 210, 218 minutes) and very low body battery readings indicate accumulated fatigue that is not being adequately managed. The nearest race is the 5K Open Water Swim on October 25th, just 8 days away, which should be the immediate priority — the good news is the 5.2km open water swim on October 3rd shows swim capability is present, but recovery before race day is critical.
suggestions: Prioritise sleep above all else this week — with multiple nights under 3.5 hours recorded recently and race day on October 25th, aim for 7–8 hours nightly; this will do more for your race performance than any additional training session.

The October 17th long ride (80km, 240 min) is a very heavy session just 8 days before an open water swim race — cap it at 60km or 150 minutes at pure Z2 (128–155W) and skip the Z3 Tempo blocks entirely to protect recovery.

The October 18th long run is well-adjusted in the plan at 13–14km, but given your sleep deficit, err toward the lower end (12–13km) and run at the slower end of 6:45–7:00/km to avoid digging a deeper fatigue hole.

Your running HR of 169 bpm at 6:15/km pace on September 25th indicates your aerobic base is under stress — for the marathon target (113 days away), prioritise consistent easy Z2 running volume over the coming weeks rather than interval intensity until your sleep and recovery normalise.

In the week after the October 25th swim race (Wk19), respect the recovery structure fully — avoid pushing the October 31st 90km ride or November 1st long run unless body battery and sleep have meaningfully recovered to 70+ and 7+ hours respectively.
